Action Plan:
1. Arrange face-to-face clinic visit for full abdominal ± pelvic examination; patient instructed to ring the support line today to book the appointment.
2. Patient to perform a urine pregnancy test today and telephone immediately if the result is positive.
3. Provide clear safety-net: attend ED or call service sooner if pain intensifies, new vomiting, shoulder-tip pain, syncope, fever, or inability to keep fluids down.
4. Ensure amoxicillin allergy is recorded in medical record.
5. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• 23-year-old female presents with constant, worsening lower-midline abdominal pain for “a few days,” severity 8/10.  
• Pain location: below umbilicus, midline, present all the time, worsening.  
• Associated symptoms: light pink vaginal bleeding since period ended 2 weeks ago, occasional nausea (no vomiting), constipation last week (now resolved), small amount of vaginal discharge.  
• Denies fever, chills, dyspnea, shoulder pain, syncope, dysuria, hematuria, weight loss, recent travel (<1 yr), or trauma.  
• Last menstrual period: 2–3 weeks ago; usually irregular with etonogestrel implant.  
• Sexual activity: regular intercourse; last 4 days ago.  
• Contraception: etonogestrel implant (in situ 1 year).  
• Home urine pregnancy test: negative 1 month ago (none since onset of pain).  
• Past medical history: no chronic disease, no surgeries, no previous pregnancies.  
• Allergies: amoxicillin (reaction details not provided).  
• Medications: etonogestrel implant; no others documented.  
• Social: school teacher; lives with husband and his family; non-smoker; denies alcohol and recreational drugs.

Objective:
• Tele-consultation – no physical examination performed.  
• No vitals available.  
• No investigations performed yet.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Lower abdominal pain:
   – Assessment / likely diagnosis: Suspected ectopic pregnancy (DDx item “Ectopic pregnancy” – High).  
   – Differential diagnoses:  
     • Ectopic pregnancy (High) – must be ruled out urgently.  
     • Pelvic inflammatory disease (Medium) – supports: lower pain, bleeding, discharge; opposes: no fever.  
     • Ovarian torsion / hemorrhagic cyst (Medium) – constant severe pain, reproductive age; pain not clearly unilateral.  
     • Appendicitis (Low) – progressive pain, nausea; opposes: midline, no fever.  
     • Constipation-related pain (Low) – constipation resolved yet pain persists.  
   – Investigations planned: Urine pregnancy test today; in-person abdominal/pelvic examination (further tests such as pelvic ultrasound or labs may be ordered at that visit).  
   – Treatment planned: None initiated remotely; safety-net advice given.  
   – Relevant referrals: Face-to-face clinic appointment arranged via support line.

2. Abnormal light vaginal bleeding:
   – Assessment / likely diagnosis: Undifferentiated abnormal uterine/pelvic bleeding – needs evaluation to exclude ectopic pregnancy (DDx “Ectopic pregnancy” – High) and PID (Medium).  
   – Differential diagnosis: same list as above plus hormonal implant irregular bleeding (DDx “Hormonal-implant side effects”).  
   – Investigations planned: Same urine pregnancy test; pelvic exam at clinic.  
   – Treatment planned: Pending evaluation results.  
   – Relevant referrals: Included in clinic appointment above.

3. Nausea:
   – Assessment / likely diagnosis: Likely secondary to pelvic/abdominal pathology above.  
   – Differential diagnosis: As per Issue 1 list.  
   – Investigations planned: None separately.  
   – Treatment planned: Symptomatic management to be addressed after primary cause identified.

Quality checks:
• Missing expected elements: vital signs, abdominal & pelvic examination findings, current medication list (other than implant), detailed allergy reaction, analgesia use, recent pregnancy test result.  
• No conflicts noted between transcript and DDx.  
• Transcript quality: several inaudible segments and incomplete sentences, but core clinical information intact.
